name: Specific Applications and Integrators
text:
# Specific Applications and Integrators

Also called: X-Ray Rendering

## Overview
This family encompasses specialized integrators and rendering modes that deviate from [standard front-to-back compositing](#1141-front-to-back-compositing-unpremultiplied.md) to address specific application requirements, such as projective diagnostic imaging [S1, unofficial], medical photo-realism [S10], interactive shading approximations [15337-shading-and-occlusion-models.md], and neural [scene composition](#11397-scene-composition.md) [11182-compositional-rendering.md]. Unlike standard [Direct Volume Ray Casting](#19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md) [19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md], which simulates light transport via the [volume rendering equation](#2098-volume-rendering-equation.md), these methods either simplify the integration (summing samples) [S1, unofficial], extend it to full path tracing ([Cinematic Rendering](#9473-cinematic-rendering.md)) [S3, unofficial][S10], approximate global illumination via occlusion buffers ([Shading and Occlusion Models](#15337-shading-and-occlusion-models.md)) [15337-shading-and-occlusion-models.md], or decouple object insertion in neural fields ([Compositional Rendering](#11182-compositional-rendering.md)) [11182-compositional-rendering.md].

## Shared principles
The methods in this family build on the foundational mechanism of Direct Volume Ray Casting [19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md], including [ray definition](#22009-projection-and-ray-geometry.md), [sampling, interpolation](#21959-interpolation.md), and transfer function mapping [S1, unofficial]. However, they diverge in the **[Compositing](#2436-compositing.md) (Integration)** step (Step 4 of the parent's Shared principles) [S1, unofficial]. While standard DVR uses the front-to-back accumulation equation, specific applications modify this accumulation:
*   **Summation:** Some modes simply sum interpolated scalar values, as in X-ray rendering [S1, unofficial].
*   **Path Tracing:** Others trace randomized photon paths to solve the multi-dimensional rendering equation, accounting for scattering and global illumination [S3, unofficial][S10].
*   **Layered Compositing:** Some render distinct material styles into separate layers and composite them post-hoc [S2].

## Subtopics

### [TVAM Integrator](6814-tvam-integrator.md)
A base class for volumetric additive manufacturing integrators that handles projector ray sampling, time sampling, and regular versus stochastic sampling modes. It sets itself apart from sibling integrators by focusing on the temporal and geometric sampling of projector emissions rather than material compositing. Choose this method when simulating volumetric additive manufacturing processes requiring precise projector emission sampling.

### [Cinematic Rendering](9473-cinematic-rendering.md)
A physically based, real-time volume rendering technique for medical image data (CT/MRI) that solves the multi-dimensional, non-continuous rendering equation by integrating light scattered from all possible directions along a ray. It sets itself apart by tracing hundreds or thousands of photon paths per pixel to simulate complex light-matter interactions, including [multiple scattering](#12474-multiple-scattering.md) and global illumination effects like soft shadows. Choose this method when photo-realistic medical visualization with accurate lighting is required.

### [Compositional Rendering](11182-compositional-rendering.md)
A method for integrating newly generated 3D objects into an existing [Neural Radiance Field (NeRF)](#834-neural-radiance-field-nerf.md) scene by decoupling the rendering of the object from the background scene. It sets itself apart by performing the final [alpha-blending](#5750-alpha-blending.md) in image space using a pre-computed scene cache, rather than accumulating the entire scene in a single ray-casting pass. Choose this method when occlusion-aware compositing of dynamic objects into static neural scenes is needed.

### [Shading and Occlusion Models](15337-shading-and-occlusion-models.md)
A family that extends Direct Volume Ray Casting by modifying the compositing step to incorporate lighting, shadows, and occlusion cues, thereby enhancing depth perception and visual clarity. It sets itself apart by using simplified or image-space techniques rather than full physically-based surface/volume [interaction](#41-interaction.md) models. Choose this method when interactive volume rendering requires enhanced depth cues without the computational cost of full global illumination.

### [WYSIWYP (What You See Is What You Pick)](16498-wysiwyp-what-you-see-is-what-you-pick.md)
A volume picking technique that enables users to intuitively select 3D spatial positions in volumetric renderings based solely on the volume data, transfer function, and visibility perception. It sets itself apart by analyzing the derivative of accumulated opacity to detect visible structures for interaction, rather than integrating color and opacity for display. Choose this method when precise 3D [spatial selection](#20933-spatial-selection.md) in interactive volume visualization is required.

### [Auditory Volume Rendering](18941-auditory-volume-rendering.md)
A rendering technique that maps scalar field values to auditory properties (pitch, amplitude, duration) using an auditory transfer function, generating sound via a ray-marching procedure similar to optical volume rendering. It sets itself apart by outputting auditory data instead of visual images. Choose this method for audio-visual data exploration or accessibility applications.

### [Spherical Coordinate Ray-Casting Volume Rendering](19598-spherical-coordinate-ray-casting-volume-rendering.md)
A ray-casting method to visualize 3D power volumetric data of EME on a globe, handling non-regular grid data organized in spherical coordinates. It sets itself apart by supporting spherical coordinate systems instead of [Cartesian grids](#3-dense-grids-and-memory-layout.md). Choose this method for geospatial or spherical volumetric data visualization.

### [All-in-Focus Neural Radiance Fields](19657-all-in-focus-neural-radiance-fields.md)
A framework to synthesize all-in-focus (AiF) novel views from dual-camera image pairs (main and ultra-wide) where the main camera has consistent defocus blur due to fixed autofocus on a prominent object. It sets itself apart by explicitly handling consistent defocus blur to produce sharp, all-in-focus novel views. Choose this method when generating sharp novel views from defocused dual-camera captures is required.

### [PRT-based Volume Rendering Approximation](19776-prt-based-volume-rendering-approximation.md)
A method to approximate in-scattering in volume rendering using [Precomputed Radiance Transfer (PRT)](#9429-precomputed-radiance-transfer-prt.md) and [Spherical Harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md) (SH) to replace expensive double integrals with dot products and cube map lookups. It sets itself apart by using PRT/SH approximations instead of direct integration or path tracing. Choose this method when real-time [in-scattering approximation](#2215-in-scattering-approximation.md) is needed without full path tracing costs.

### [Texture-Enhanced Direct Volume Rendering](20022-texture-enhanced-direct-volume-rendering.md)
A methodology for [direct volume rendering](#1184-direct-volume-rendering.md) that extends the standard color-opacity transfer function process by enabling the use of textures to encode additional information (e.g., fiber direction, cellular abnormalities) throughout the volume in three dimensions. It sets itself apart by integrating volumetric textures instead of just scalar values. Choose this method when rich, multi-channel volumetric data visualization is required.

### [True Volume Aurora](20150-true-volume-aurora.md)
A volume rendering method for aurorae based on a height-based model, GPU-friendly atmosphere model, efficient [ray marching](#6739-ray-marching.md) with distance fields, and interactive frame rates. It sets itself apart by using a physically-based electron deposition function and spline-based footprint simulation. Choose this method for real-time, physically accurate aurora visualization.

### Two Level Volume Rendering with Layers
A technique that achieves results similar to traditional [two-level volume rendering](#7677-two-level-volume-rendering.md) by rendering different styles (e.g., different transfer functions or rendering modes like MIP vs DVR) into separate [layers and compositing](#4539-multi-layer-surface-compositing.md) them, rather than selecting rendering types per ray segment during integration [S2].
*   **Step:** Render each distinct material [style or transfer function](#777-style-transfer-function-1d.md) into a separate layer (e.g., DVR for soft tissue, DVR for bones) [S2]. Composite the separate layers into a final image using a compositing function that maps the resulting layers to the view volume [S2].
*   **Parameter:** Opacity: Layers can be assigned specific opacity values during rendering or compositing (e.g., layer 1 opacity 0.4, layer 3 opacity 0.1, layer 2 opacity 0.5) [S2].
*   **Comparison:** Unlike original two-level volume rendering which composites segments in the order the ray encounters materials (e.g., $I = A_1 B_1 A_2 B_2$), this method composites all segments of the same material separately first, then composites the intermediate results (e.g., $I = A_1 A_2 A_3 B_1 B_2$) [S2].

### Volumetric Ray Tracing Framework (Sobierajski/Kaufman)
A complete framework for volumetric ray tracing developed by Sobierajski and Kaufman that includes global illumination effects (shadows, reflections, light interaction between volumetric/geometric objects) and volumetric rendering effects (fog, transparency) [S3, unofficial]. It was incorporated into VolVis, a comprehensive volume visualization system developed at Stony Brook University [S3, unofficial].

### Pseudo-depth Feature Rendering
A method to render features for a 3D scene representation (InstantNGP) by computing a pseudo-depth [surface and sampling](#11356-surface-based-sampling.md) features locally around it, avoiding full volume rendering for computational efficiency [S4].
*   **Step:** Compute the pseudo depth of the surface as a weighted average of the depth of each sampled point in volume rendering [S4]. Compute the feature in five points around the pseudo surface point by adding small perturbations during training and inference [S4]. When optimizing the scene with CLIPNeRF, backpropagate gradients to only the rays selected by the target text label (e.g., 'apple'), rather than all rays [S4].
*   **Parameter:** Number of feature sampling points: 5 points around the pseudo surface point [S4].
*   **Pitfall:** The method is described as 'very efficient but works for training the [distilled feature field](#12026-distilled-feature-fields.md)', implying it may not be suitable for final inference or high-fidelity rendering compared to full volume rendering [S4].

### Stereoscopic Rendering
Rendering from multiple viewpoints (offset by a fixed [rotation](#19376-rotation.md)) to enhance user perception of depth features, used for live stereoscopic display [S5]. Stereoscopic rendering required an additional 2.5ms computational cost on the NVIDIA GTX Titan Black GPU [S5].

## Background
The concept of specific integration modes originated with the distinction between "X-ray" rendering (simple summation) and "full" volume rendering (light transport simulation) in early volume visualization overviews [S1, unofficial]. The "Two Level Volume Rendering" concept was formalized to handle multi-material datasets, with later variations introducing layered compositing to decouple material styles [S2]. Cinematic Rendering emerged in the medical imaging domain to provide photo-realistic, clinically accurate visualizations by incorporating global illumination via path tracing [S3, unofficial][S10]. Shading and Occlusion Models provide ambient occlusion-like cues in interactive volume rendering without the cost of full global illumination [15337-shading-and-occlusion-models.md]. Compositional Rendering decouples object and scene rendering for neural fields [11182-compositional-rendering.md]. The Sobierajski/Kaufman framework represents an early comprehensive system integrating volumetric ray tracing with geometric global illumination [S3, unofficial].
